packets.title: Additive migration on an existing populated store

gate.red_expect: GATE XS1 RED: opening a populated store rewrote an existing row

regression: cd mcp-server && npx biome check src/
acceptance: A copy of ~/repos/axiomdb/.amanuensis/memory.db is taken to temporary storage; the source is opened read-only and never written (decisions.md §6).

Opening the copy runs runMigrations and initializeSchema and creates every table this lane adds, with no existing dispositions, evidence, file_ledger or vocabulary row altered or deleted — asserted by a row-level digest taken before and after.
A second open of the same copy succeeds: every new CREATE carries IF NOT EXISTS (spec.md §3.2).
Each new table's immutability and no-delete triggers fire on the copy: an UPDATE and a DELETE both raise.

The copy's 54 unattached dispositions do not vanish; the next advance of a subsystem holding one is refused with the §2.3 message, and materialize_docs(clean_publish=true) leaves the previous output untouched on that red (ADR-0005).
The gate reports cannot run, not green, when the AxiomDB store is unreadable on this machine.
packets.notes: GATE XS1 runs the migration on a copy of the AxiomDB store (166 dispositions, 54 unattached, 295 ledger rows, 1718 gaps); the source is copied, never opened for writing, and digested before and after. Red on S2: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS is a silent no-op when the name is held by an object of another kind, so an open could leave a declared table absent and report success; openDatabase now runs requireSchemaObjects over schema.sql's own 517 declarations, which covers each table P2-P4 adds the moment it is declared, with no second list. Two acceptance bullets are not P0's to make green and are not asserted here: 'every table this lane adds' is the empty set at P0, so S1 asserts the stronger schema-wide form instead, and the SS2.3 advance refusal for an unattached disposition is P1's deliverable (invariants.ts) - P1's regression list already re-runs this gate. M5 asserts the 54 unattached dispositions survive; P1 asserts the refusal. T2 proves the append-only pair behaviourally on 46 of 75 declared tables; the other 29 refuse this probe's generic seed for named cross-row reasons, reported in the gate's notes.

packets.title: Evidence-backed dispositions

gate.red_expect: GATE SD1 RED: a disposition was answered from nothing

regression: cd mcp-server && npx biome check src/
acceptance: set_disposition requires evidence_ids with at least one existing id and writes dispositions plus disposition_evidence in one transaction (spec.md §2.2).
A refused set_disposition leaves neither the disposition nor any attachment behind.
evidence_quality stronger than the strongest attached kind is refused with the §2.2 message.

enforcePhasePrerequisites refuses concerns/adversarial/mapped for a subsystem holding a disposition with no attached row, and separately for one whose attached ref_sha does not resolve (spec.md §2.3).
The gate ships a must-stay-green control: a subsystem whose dispositions are all attached advances.
The gate header states the vacuity at the advance to concerns (spec.md §8.1).
No existing store is migrated, backfilled or rewritten (spec.md §2.4).

The distinct ref_sha values of the named evidence rows are resolved in one batched git cat-file --batch-check, not one resolveWorkspaceCommit per id (spec.md §2.2); test-perf-ceilings.mjs stays green.

All nine existing set_disposition call sites pass evidence_ids and stay green: test-invariants, test-residual-hardening, test-perf-ceilings, test-vocabulary-source, test-perf-tier2, test-consumer-route, test-cloud-e2e, test-smoke, dev/test-rebuild-regeneration.
A disposition with one resolvable and one unresolvable attachment advances; the unresolvable one is reported, not refused (spec.md §2.3).
The gate's red commit ships the complete test against the unchanged implementation and prints GATE SD1 RED with no crash signature (spec.md §8.0).
packets.notes: GATE SD1 ships 21 assertions: set_disposition's four refusals with nothing left behind, the one-transaction write proved by a probe trigger that refuses the attachment, the §2.3 advance refusal at all three rungs and through both status doors and enforcePhasePrerequisites directly, the mixed resolvable/unreachable control that advances and reports, and C37's batching measured with a git shim on PATH. Three choices the spec left open: helpers.ts gains resolveWorkspaceCommits (no packet owns that file; it is the honest home beside the singular form's ceiling comment) and subsystems.ts passes the workspace and surfaces the reported lines (no packet lists it either, and the check cannot reach git without it); the §2.4 sentence about materialize_docs is read as P2's, since §3.3a specifies the publication predicate and P2 owns materialize.ts. test-consumer-route names set_disposition only in prose and its write-tool list, so it has no call site and is green unchanged. The gate's E8 was vacuous at the red commit (its second call over-claimed and was refused by the ladder before reaching the write) and was fixed in b3d226c; it now requires the refusal to be the probe trigger's own and turns red when db.transaction is removed. dev/test-rebuild-regeneration.mjs still reports one failure, over design/reader-lenses/rebuild-coverage-receipt.json's registry_ownership; its inputs are byte-identical to the packet's start commit, so it predates P1 — it is in completion.commands, not in any packet's regression list.

packets.title: Scope reconciliation before authority

gate.red_expect: GATE SR1 RED: the store was not reconciled at the published revision

regression: cd mcp-server && npx biome check src/
acceptance: detect_changes writes exactly one append-only scope_reconciliations row per invocation, inside the transaction that rewrites scope_gaps (spec.md §3.2).
The row's counts agree with a re-derivation from git ls-files in the fixture repository.
Reconciled-at-R is the three-condition predicate of spec.md §3.3 and a reconciliation at A does not satisfy a publication at B.
The advance to mapped and materialize_docs both refuse an unreconciled store with the §3.3 messages; the advance to structural does not.
Control: a reconciled store advances and publishes.
initializeSchema creates scope_reconciliations on the next open of an existing store with no row rewritten; REQUIRED_VIEWS is untouched because the change adds no view (src/db.ts:44, :61-82, :84-89).

The DDL uses CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS throughout and ships scope_reconciliation_is_immutable and scope_reconciliation_cannot_be_deleted; the trigger, not the prose, is what makes the table append-only.
detect_changes enumerates git ls-tree -r --name-only at the resolved revision, not git ls-files, and stores tree_digest and ledger_digest beside the counts.
Reconciled-at-R re-derives both digests, so a reconciliation goes stale as soon as the ledger is mutated under it.
materialize_docs and the fully-surveyed predicate additionally refuse a reconciliation reporting nonzero unledgered or absent (spec.md §3.3a); the advance to mapped does not.
The gate seeds duplicate ledger ownership, a correct-but-nonzero gap, index/tree divergence, an abbreviated sha, and a stale reconciliation after ledger mutation (spec.md §8.2).
packets.notes: GATE SR1 ships 22 assertions over the real tools: the append-only record and its atomicity with the scope_gaps rewrite (proved by a probe trigger that refuses the insert, aimed at a new commit carrying a new unledgered path so an escaped write is visible in both scope_gaps and last_checked_sha), the counts and both digests re-derived from git ls-tree, UPDATE and DELETE refused by the schema's own triggers, an abbreviated revision resolved rather than string-matched in both directions, duplicate ledger ownership reported, index/tree divergence resolved towards the tree in both directions, an earlier revision's tree enumerated at that revision, a standing reconciliation lost to a ledger mutation and restored by a fresh detect_changes, forged tree and ledger digests refused, the two refusals with their messages, the table's arrival on an existing store's next open with no domain row rewritten, and three controls: structural does not refuse, mapped stands on a correct but nonzero unledgered, and a reconciled complete store advances and publishes for real. One deviation, recorded rather than made silently: spec.md:506 tells the reader `get_scope_gaps names them` and no such tool exists anywhere in the repository, so the refusal names detect_changes' own unledgered_paths and absent_ledger_paths. Three gaps filled: ledger_digest is over (path, classification) pairs one per row as §3.2 words it, so moving one row between subsystems with an unchanged classification is the single ledger mutation a standing reconciliation survives (recorded in the gate header as a false green it cannot exclude); `exempt` counts distinct paths, being one side of a tracked-set intersection, while `absent` stays a count of rows as §3.2 words it; and duplicate ownership, which neither scope_gaps kind can record, is reported in detect_changes' result capped at 25 named paths with the count kept. requireCompleteReconciliation is exported for §5.5's fully-surveyed predicate, which is P4's to wire — P2 delivers only the materialize_docs half. Six files outside P2's deliverables had to learn the new prerequisite, none of them weakened: test-invariants.mjs and test-disposition-evidence.mjs (P1's) reconcile before the advance to mapped, test-projection-custody.mjs ledgers its one tracked path and reconciles before publishing, dev/test-rebuild-regeneration.mjs reconciles before the advance its check admits, DEVELOPMENT.md is regenerated for two changed tool descriptions, and test-refresh-recovery.mjs's zero-impact fixture now removes an unledgered path instead of adding one, because execute_refresh_run ends in a publication and §3.3a cannot publish a tree carrying a path nobody assigned or excluded. The rebuild packets should expect the same of the operational scripts that publish — dev/promote-docs.mjs, dev/record-regeneration-pass.mjs, dev/run-codex-host-harness.mjs and dev/adopt-codex-host-evidence.mjs all call materialize_docs and now need a standing, clean reconciliation at HEAD before they will publish.

packets.title: Vocabulary: discharge or decline

gate.red_expect: GATE VD1 RED: a subsystem reached structural having neither defined a term nor declined

regression: cd mcp-server && npx biome check src/
acceptance: define_term requires an active session, parses first_seen with requireWorkspaceCitation(strict), resolves the token's revision, and verifies the token's path exists in that revision's tree with git cat-file -e (spec.md §4.2).
vocabulary_declinations is append-only and decline_domain_vocabulary refuses a subsystem that already has an anchored term (spec.md §4.3).
The advance to structural refuses a subsystem with neither an anchored term scoped to it nor a declination; a codebase-wide term does not satisfy it (spec.md §4.4).
Control: a subsystem with one anchored term advances, and so does one with only a declination.
The declination kind is declared in contracts/conspectus-vocabulary.json and both gen-vocabulary checks pass.
No numeric minimum is introduced anywhere: one term is enough and none is a legitimate answer.
Scoping is per (term, subsystem): re-defining a shared term cannot silently revoke another subsystem's discharge (spec.md §4.4).
The declination the prerequisite reads is the effective one, whose ref_sha still resolves; older rows are history and discharge nothing.
vocabulary_declinations ships its immutability and no-delete triggers and CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS.
decline_domain_vocabulary is registered in src/index.ts and gen-tool-inventory.mjs --check passes over a regenerated DEVELOPMENT.md; a tool declared but not advertised is a finding.
gen-vocabulary.mjs regenerates src/vocabulary.ts and materializer/amanuensis_materializer/vocabulary.py and both --check and --check-sql pass.
packets.notes: Scoping uses §4.4's primary fix, the vocabulary_scopes join table, not the narrower refusal fallback: vocabulary.subsystem_id stays the primary scope, define_term carries a pre-join-table row's scope into the table before its upsert moves that column, and list_vocabulary now reads the scope set. Gaps filled and recorded here: first_seen is stored with the path normalized and the revision resolved to 40 hex (§4.2 says that only of ref_sha); the effective declination is the newest row whose ref_sha resolves, so a later unreachable row does not un-discharge an intact earlier one; decline_domain_vocabulary's optional session_id must name the active session; and the contract gains a vocabulary_discharge enum (terms/declined/not-recorded) so §4.5's three states have one source in both languages. Nine other files' fixtures now discharge before advancing to structural (test-invariants, test-smoke, test-phase2-claims-gate, test-cloud-e2e, both perf tests, dev/test-rebuild-regeneration and the P1/P2 gates) and test-residual-hardening declares the new enum a non-input; nothing was weakened, and dev/test-rebuild-regeneration is back to its single pre-existing §8.10 failure.

packets.title: Findings carry forward across a reinitialization

gate.red_expect: GATE CF1 RED: a carried finding has no terminal outcome

regression: cd mcp-server && npx biome check src/
acceptance: carried_findings and carried_finding_outcomes exist with the shapes of spec.md §5.2, outside the findings namespace.
archived_store_id is derived as spec.md §5.3 and separates the baseline store from the candidate store.
rebuild-self-conspectus-store.mjs requires --carry-from and accepts either an archived store or an export; --carry-from none records an explicit reasoned empty carry.
record_carried_outcome enforces the three outcomes' authority rules (spec.md §5.4), one outcome per record, and no deletion.
The fully-surveyed predicate gains clause 7 and emits the obligation id carried:<store>:<id>; it is not enforced at mapped.
dev/pecia-resolve-finding.mjs follows the §5.7 lookup order, keeps exit codes 0/1/2, and never prints its argument.
Control: a store whose carried records all carry terminal outcomes is fully surveyed on clause 7.
carried_finding_evidence and carry_runs are declared with the other two tables; all four use CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS and ship their immutability and no-delete triggers.
archived_store_id is a minted store_generation, or store-legacy- over a frozen archive's git_state; an export without archived_store_id is refused as a carry source (spec.md §5.3).
--carry-from none requires --carry-reason and writes a carry_runs row; expected_count and imported_count are recorded separately and a carry refuses to finish while they differ.
A finding the archive had already closed is pre-recorded archived-terminal, which only the carry writes; record_carried_outcome refuses it.
repaired requires the attached evidence revision to be a descendant of or equal to repaired_sha, tested with git merge-base --is-ancestor.
attach_carried_evidence and list_carried_findings are registered in src/index.ts; the list tool pages within the 8192-byte envelope budget and the carried count is read back from a third process.

dev/check-store-fully-surveyed.mjs evaluates an open store read-only and carries clause 7 over a nonempty undecided set; dev/check-living-conspectus.mjs still reads the frozen A0 fixture and is not retargeted.
dev/test-rebuild-readback.mjs passes --carry-from none --carry-reason in both driver arms, asserts the carry_runs row was written, and keeps a separate missing-argument refusal case.
GATE CF2 lives here, where dev/pecia-resolve-finding.mjs's change can turn it red; an id matching carried records from two archives exits 2.
packets.notes: Carried findings live in carried_findings/carried_finding_outcomes/carried_finding_evidence/carry_runs plus a new single-row store_identity, all five CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS with immutability and no-delete trigger pairs. Three gaps the spec left open were filled and are the things to look at first. (1) carry_runs is immutable by its own trigger, so imported_count cannot be incremented across calls; the carry is therefore three tools — begin_carry_run declares expected_count and imported_count, carry_finding refuses past imported_count, finish_carry_run refuses while expected, imported and the rows written disagree. (2) --carry-reason is required for every source kind, not only for none, because carry_runs.reason is NOT NULL for every kind. (3) §5.3's export-versus-store cross-check had no second input under a single --carry-from, so the driver gained --carry-verify-store <path>; a carry from a store records itself as its own witness. archivedStoreId separates three states, not two: no store_identity table selects the legacy derivation, a table with no row is refused rather than silently given a second identity. dev/check-store-fully-surveyed.mjs evaluates ADR-0001 clauses 1-4 and 7 from the store and reports clauses 5 and 6 unevaluable — never satisfied — when the store records no composition run or projection verification. Eighteen sabotages were run against the implementation; four survived and each named a gate gap now closed (the driver refusals must arrive before the discard; C7 writes exactly imported_count so only the expected/imported comparison can fire; A7 carries through the tool and reads findings; D8 and D9 read idx_carried_outcome_one and the current-session half of the successor rule). GATE CF2 ships and is proved here, green under five sabotages of its own.

packets.title: The depth gate and its frozen baseline

gate.red_expect: GATE D1 RED: the depth gate did not turn red on a seeded

regression: cd mcp-server && npx biome check src/
acceptance: dev/survey-depth-baseline.json carries the D1-D12 SQL verbatim, the archived store identity and anchor, and the thirteen baseline open finding ids; it is regenerable and --checkable.
dev/test-survey-depth.mjs turns red on each of B1-B6 seeded independently (spec.md §7.3) and green on the must-stay-green control store.
The gate reports RED, never green, when the baseline fixture is absent or unreadable.
Every fraction is printed with its denominator; a zero denominator is out of band.
The reported axes (D1, D4, D5, D6, D7%, D8, D9, D10, D11 and the histograms) are printed with signed deltas and turn nothing red.
Both arms exist: a baseline arm over the fixture and a candidate arm over the live store or the acceptance receipt, asserting agreement when both are present.
The gate runs in .github/workflows/test.yml.
The exempt set of D2 is derived from conspectus-vocabulary.json's obligation_bearing field; a deferred-with-reason path is obligation-bearing, and a regression asserts it.
B1 requires zero unledgered and zero absent at the acceptance revision, not merely a recorded count that matches the tree (spec.md §7.3).
The candidate arm exits 2 cannot run with neither a live store nor a committed receipt, and GATE D1 asserts that state rather than green.
record-survey-depth-baseline.mjs --check exits 2, never 0, when the archived store is unreadable; it is in this packet's regression list and in completion.commands.
Every blocking verdict is recomputed from the receipt's row-level witnesses, never read from a recorded verdict field.
packets.notes: Attempt 1's implementation is unchanged; the only edit is the status line dev/test-survey-depth-red-gates.mjs prints. It now leads with the packet marker spec.md 8.0 clauses 1-2 bind the launcher to and carries D1's verdict as its reason — 'GATE P5 RED: GATE D1 RED: ...' and 'GATE P5 GREEN — GATE D1 GREEN' — so gate.red_expect, which 8.0 says quotes the first line of the reason, still matches unchanged. The red was re-proved on top at 4c97944 rather than by rewriting c07ffe7: it carries the corrected gate over a tree where the three deliverables are absent and neither gate is in CI, and all 32 assertions fire (two more than c07ffe7, which predates the two added in a6f0815). REVIEWER, FIRST: the same collision is latent for P10. spec.md:1081 fixes D0's single last line as 'GATE D0 GREEN|RED|CANNOT RUN', spec.md:1284-1286 binds the launcher to 'GATE <packet-id>', and P10's gate command is dev/test-survey-depth.mjs — so P10 will be refused exactly as P5 was unless D0's line leads with 'GATE P10 '. Fixing it there also means updating D1's ten 'GATE D0 ' prefix assertions and the '^GATE D0 GREEN' and '^GATE D0 CANNOT RUN: ' greps in .github/workflows/test.yml. Not fixed here: at P5 D0 is a deliverable, not the packet gate, so no packet marker is correct on its line yet.

packets.title: The projection renders 'not measured'

gate.red_expect: GATE PM1 RED: an unreconciled store rendered a coverage number

acceptance: _tracked_paths reads the standing reconciliation and returns None (not 0) for an unreconciled store (spec.md §3.4).
The overview's 'Paths in scope with no ledger row' and 'Files read, of those carrying an obligation' print 'not measured' with the revision and the reason when unreconciled.
'Not yet surveyed' section 1 routes an unreconciled store into the existing _gap_denominator sentence with the revision named.
A declined subsystem renders its reason, session and revision; 'declined' and 'not recorded' are distinct and never collapsed (spec.md §4.5).
The read-back's coverage axis counts a 'not measured' row as present-and-honest, never as a satisfied coverage claim, and no read-back axis is weakened.

Two controls: a reconciled store with zero unledgered paths renders byte-identically to today against a committed fixture, and a reconciled store with unledgered > 0 renders against the new denominator with the old value recorded in the gate header as the intended change.
Where a subsystem holds both anchored terms and a declination, the terms render as current and the declination beneath them as superseded history (spec.md §4.5).

spec.md §5.6's Carried obligations section renders on the Unresolved lens and the History pages in both formats, and readback.py gains a carried-record census beside _finding_partition_census, _ledger_stale_census and _locus_index_census.
Carried defects undecided is its own overview row and is never summed into Findings open.
The gate seeds a state, a coverage and a content fault against the carried markers.
packets.notes: Denominators: the overview's Files read is now D3 of D2 over the standing reconciliation (spec §1.2) — distinct examined ledger paths the tree still carries, over tracked_paths minus exempt — so both halves count paths, not rows; §3.4 named only the denominator, and counting examined *rows* against tracked *paths* would double-count a path two subsystems both examined. REVIEWER, FIRST: (1) §3.4 does not say what a read-only projection does when git cannot enumerate the tree at R, so readback.reconciliation_standing evaluates §3.3 conditions 2, 3 and 5 always and condition 4 only when the bound workspace answers; where it cannot, the row's own ledger_digest and recorded revision are what the reading stands on. Named in the gate header and in the function's docstring; GATE SR1 owns whether a written reconciliation was correct. (2) Two files outside the deliverables changed and neither is weakened: html_projection.py's durable-marker allow-list was a hard-coded alternation that stripped the carried marker out of the HTML, so it now derives from readback.MARKER_KINDS (§5.6 requires both formats); and test-overview-truthfulness.py and test-lens-pages.py each gained the scope_reconciliations row their coverage assertions now read from — the overview's Files-read denominator moves 3 -> 4 there, the intended change, differing by exactly the unledgered count. (3) §5.6 leaves open whether both lenses list every carried record or partition them; they are partitioned by decidedness — undecided on Unresolved, decided on History — which is §6.2's existing one-full-record-per-page rule and is what lets the new census count exactly one marker per corpus. (4) The overview's Carried defects undecided row is published when carry_runs or carried_findings is non-empty and omitted when neither is, so a store nobody ran a carry against does not report 0 (§5.2, VP4(e)). (5) The red was re-proved at 104b69b with the finished gate over the tree as P6 found it; eaec992 is the first red and carried an earlier draft of two arms.

packets.title: Skill parity and the refusal-parity check

gate.red_expect: GATE RP1 RED: the parity check passed with a registered phrase missing

regression: cd mcp-server && npx biome check src/
acceptance: Each of the eleven passages in spec.md §6.1 states the server's refusal in the server's own words; nothing describing a surviving behaviour is removed or softened.
contracts/refusal-parity.json registers all four new refusals plus the two existing ones this lane touches.
check-refusal-parity.mjs fails naming the entry id and the side that lost the phrase, and runs in CI beside check-evidence-vocabulary.mjs.
The gate proves the check turns red when a registered phrase is deleted from a reference and, separately, from the server file.
Control: the register at HEAD passes.
The gate header states that a refusal nobody registers drifts freely (spec.md §8.7).
check-refusal-parity.mjs derives a candidate refusal set from the server's own ToolError messages and reports every one with no register entry; the derived set is empty at HEAD.
phase-1-scope.md:58, phase-2-structural.md:24 and phase-3-concerns.md:120 each carry the define_term anchor obligation; the derived check is what found them.
packets.notes: Sixteen register entries, not six: the derived scan reports every thrown or returned refusal opening 'cannot advance', '<tool> refuses:' or '<tool> requires', and the acceptance requires that set to be empty, so the nine status-ladder sentences, the publication refusal, the active-session requirement, set_disposition's evidence_ids, the declination conflict and define_term's anchor are registered beside the four new refusals and the two existing ones §6.1 names. The reference-side scan found three callers past §6.1's eleven passages — phase-5-packaging.md, subsystem-survey.md and memory-audit.md all instruct materialize_docs or the advance to mapped — and each now states the refusal, per §6.1's own rule that an affected caller is one wherever it lives. Two scope choices the spec left open, both with fixture controls (G4): the subject of a 'refuses:'/'requires' opening must be an advertised tool or an interpolation, and the message must be thrown or returned rather than collected into another call (which is what excludes refresh.ts:814's blockers.push). Both sides of every comparison have whitespace collapsed, because the server wraps a refusal across four concatenated literals and the references wrap the same sentence at their own column limit.

packets.title: Reinitialize, carry, and onboard in the lane worktree

gate.red_expect: GATE CR1 RED: the carry receipt does not account for every archived finding

regression: cd mcp-server && npx biome check src/
acceptance: The reader-lenses §12.1 recipe runs in this worktree through step 6: snapshot, stop with an ESRCH pid probe and an lsof exclusivity check, delete, initialize and restart in a second process, carry, read back from a third. Snapshot and delete run unconditionally even though this worktree has no prior store.

The carry reads the archived store at archive/store-7c1c1a9/memory.db opened ?immutable=1 — not the export, which carries no store identity — and writes 22 carried records with a store-legacy- archived_store_id derived from its frozen git_state row.
carry_runs records source_kind='store', the path, the archived anchor, the reason, and expected_count 22 equal to imported_count 22.
The third-process read-back returns the carried count through list_carried_findings within the envelope budget.

Onboarding runs and detect_changes at HEAD writes a scope_reconciliations row whose tree_digest and ledger_digest re-derive; the calibrated concern checklist is written to mcp-server/contracts/concern-checklist.json with a --check.

design/survey-depth/carry-receipt.json records every archived finding id, its archived resolution state, and its carried_id, so the survey packet's denominator is a document this packet committed and P11 does not rewrite.
Every gate this lane has shipped is green before the packet is accepted: XS1, SD1, SR1, VD1, CF1, PM1, RP1, CF2, D1.

GATE CR1 is spec.md §8.9a: red when carry-receipt.json omits an archived finding id, names a carried_id no carried_findings row has, disagrees with the archive's resolution state, or reports a count differing from carry_runs; it reports cannot run when the archive is unreadable.
packets.notes: The §12.1 recipe ran here and the store it left is the lane worktrees .amanuensis (untracked): snapshot 059aa03, ESRCH pid probe, lsof exclusivity, delete, reinit in a second process, 22 carried records from the archived store opened ?immutable=1, read back from a third through list_carried_findings in 3 pages whose largest envelope was 8000 of 8192 bytes. Onboarding registered 9 subsystems (B-09 is new: the design lanes and their drivers), calibrated 12 concerns with T5 disqualified as an open question, and assigned all 640 tracked paths; the standing reconciliation at b716a6d is 640/640, 0 unledgered, 0 absent, 69 exempt, and both digests re-derive independently. Three files outside the deliverable list. (1) mcp-server/src/invariants.ts and src/db.ts: readArchivedStore selects resolution state from finding_state_current and the one archive §5.8 names was frozen before that view existed, so the carry could not read it at all; the view is now re-declared TEMP over the archive from schema.sqls own text, which keeps the legacy-status fallback in the single place test-finding-partition.mjs requires. It is P4s deliverable and this packet could not land without it. (2) dev/test-rebuild-coverage.mjs and dev/test-reader-lenses-dogfood.mjs: both assert their receipts rows over <repo>/.amanuensis, and both receipts name a store in the primary checkout; with a store here for the first time they compared two unrelated stores. Each live arm now reads the store its own receipt names and says so otherwise -- relabelling either receipt to name this store turns both red again on exactly the old assertions, which is the control. (3) mcp-server/scripts/check-concern-checklist.mjs is the --check §8.10 asks for, and design/survey-depth/rebuild-receipt.json holds the drivers receipt so design/reader-lenses/rebuild-receipt.json is not overwritten. Two gaps filled and recorded. The finding-id convention in the new contract is ^<subsystem-compact>-R\\d+$ rather than §8.10s quoted <subsystem-compact>-<N>: the archives ids are the latter shape and 22 of them are live carried rows, so a finding of this survey named B03-5 would shadow the obligation it inherited through §5.7s resolver. And §7.4 step 5 still says --carry-from ...old-findings-7c1c1a9.json while §5.8 step 1 and this packets acceptance say the archived store; the store is what was used, and §7.4 step 5 is the stale sentence.
